meta.name: Analyze YouTube channel performance with Telegram, Google Sheets, and Gemini

parameters.content:
## Youtube Channel Analyser

### How it works

This workflow lets a user send a YouTube channel link through Telegram, validates and resolves the channel with the YouTube Data API, then fetches recent upload and video statistics. It computes channel/video velocity metrics, builds a channel fingerprint, logs valid snapshots to Google Sheets, and uses Gemini to generate a Telegram channel analysis report. It also returns Telegram messages for bad links, missing channels, API errors, or insufficient sample size.

### Setup steps

**1. Telegram** — create a bot with BotFather, add its token as a Telegram credential, and select that same credential on the trigger and all five message nodes (Notify Bad Channel Link, Notify Channel Not Found, Notify No Baseline Found, Handle Telegram API Error, Send Channel Report).

**2. YouTube Data API v3** — enable it in Google Cloud and create an API key. In n8n add a **Query Auth** generic credential with **Name** set to `key` and **Value** set to your API key, then select it on all three HTTP Request nodes. The name must be exactly `key`, that is the query parameter the YouTube API expects.

**3. Google Sheets** — create a sheet tab whose first row holds these 12 headers, spelled exactly:
`snapshot_at`, `channel_id`, `channel_title`, `subscribers`, `total_videos`, `sample_size`, `baseline_vph`, `baseline_views_per_day`, `median_views`, `median_duration_min`, `pct_with_chapters`, `noise_floor_hit`
Then open **Append to Google Sheets** and pick your document and tab from the dropdowns. The node ships with placeholder IDs that must be replaced or the run will fail. If you use a service account credential, also share the sheet with the service account email address, otherwise every append returns a permission error.

**4. Gemini** — add a Google Gemini API credential and confirm the model in **Gemini Model Setup** is available on your account and region.

**5. Test before publishing** — run it against a large channel, a small channel, a brand new channel with no uploads, and a bad link, to confirm all four reply paths fire.

### Customization

Adjust the number of uploads fetched, the sample-size threshold, velocity/baseline formulas, Google Sheets columns, and the Gemini prompt to match the type of channel analysis you want to produce.

## Receive channel request

Starts from a Telegram message, extracts the chat and channel lookup details, and checks whether the submitted link is valid before continuing.

## Resolve channel status

Looks up the YouTube channel, branches on whether it exists, and sends Telegram responses for invalid links, API errors, or missing channels.

## Fetch recent uploads

Shapes the resolved channel profile and retrieves the latest upload playlist items, splitting the upload list into individual records.

## Request video statistics

Collects the recent video IDs, requests their detailed YouTube statistics in a batch call, and splits the returned videos for per-video processing.

## Rank video velocity

Normalizes video metrics, sorts videos by velocity, and aggregates the ranked set for channel-level calculations.

## Build channel fingerprint

Calculates baseline performance metrics and creates a compact fingerprint summarizing the channel’s recent publishing and performance characteristics.

## Validate sample logging

Checks whether the sample is large enough for analysis, logs valid snapshots to Google Sheets, or notifies the user when no reliable baseline can be created.

## Generate Telegram report

Uses Gemini to analyze the logged channel snapshot and sends the generated channel report back to the Telegram chat.

assignments.name: lookup_type
assignments.value: ={{ (function(t){ var m; if ((m = t.match(/youtube\.com\/channel\/(UC[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22})/))) return ['id', m[1]]; if ((m = t.match(/youtube\.com\/@([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)/))) return ['forHandle', '@' + m[1]]; if ((m = t.match(/youtube\.com\/user\/([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)/))) return ['forUsername', m[1]]; if ((m = t.match(/youtube\.com\/c\/([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)/))) return ['forHandle', '@' + m[1]]; if ((m = t.match(/(?:^|\s)@([A-Za-z0-9._-]{3,})/))) return ['forHandle', '@' + m[1]]; if ((m = t.match(/^\s*(UC[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22})\s*$/))) return ['id', m[1]]; return ['none', '']; })(($json.message.text || '').trim())[0] }}

assignments.value: ={{ (function(t){ var m; if ((m = t.match(/youtube\.com\/channel\/(UC[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22})/))) return ['id', m[1]]; if ((m = t.match(/youtube\.com\/@([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)/))) return ['forHandle', '@' + m[1]]; if ((m = t.match(/youtube\.com\/user\/([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)/))) return ['forUsername', m[1]]; if ((m = t.match(/youtube\.com\/c\/([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)/))) return ['forHandle', '@' + m[1]]; if ((m = t.match(/(?:^|\s)@([A-Za-z0-9._-]{3,})/))) return ['forHandle', '@' + m[1]]; if ((m = t.match(/^\s*(UC[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22})\s*$/))) return ['id', m[1]]; return ['none', '']; })(($json.message.text || '').trim())[1] }}

assignments.name: duration_sec
assignments.value: ={{ (function(d){ var m = String(d || '').match(/PT(?:(\d+)H)?(?:(\d+)M)?(?:(\d+)S)?/); if (!m) return 0; return (Number(m[1]||0)*3600)+(Number(m[2]||0)*60)+Number(m[3]||0); })($json.contentDetails ? $json.contentDetails.duration : '') }}

nodes.name: Set Velocity Baseline
nodes.notes: Median, not mean. Also flags the noise floor: under 200 median views a '2x breakout' is a handful of people, not a pattern.

assignments.name: baseline_vph
assignments.value: ={{ (function(a){ var s = a.filter(function(v){ return v.age_hours >= 48; }).map(function(v){ return v.vph; }).sort(function(x,y){ return x - y; }); if (!s.length) return 0; var m = Math.floor(s.length / 2); var med = s.length % 2 ? s[m] : (s[m-1] + s[m]) / 2; return med < 10 ? Math.round(med * 1000) / 1000 : Math.round(med * 10) / 10; })($json.videos) }}

assignments.name: median_duration_min
assignments.value: ={{ (function(a){ if (!a.length) return 0; var s = a.map(function(v){ return v.duration_sec; }).sort(function(x,y){ return x - y; }); var m = Math.floor(s.length / 2); return Math.round((s.length % 2 ? s[m] : (s[m-1] + s[m]) / 2) / 6) / 10; })($json.videos) }}

assignments.name: baseline_views_per_day
assignments.value: ={{ (function(a){ var s = a.filter(function(v){ return v.age_hours >= 48; }).map(function(v){ return v.vph; }).sort(function(x,y){ return x - y; }); if (!s.length) return 0; var m = Math.floor(s.length / 2); return Math.round((s.length % 2 ? s[m] : (s[m-1] + s[m]) / 2) * 24); })($json.videos) }}

assignments.name: median_views
assignments.value: ={{ (function(a){ var s = a.filter(function(v){ return v.age_hours >= 48; }).map(function(v){ return v.views; }).sort(function(x,y){ return x - y; }); if (!s.length) return 0; var m = Math.floor(s.length / 2); return Math.round(s.length % 2 ? s[m] : (s[m-1] + s[m]) / 2); })($json.videos) }}

assignments.name: noise_floor_hit
assignments.value: ={{ (function(a){ var s = a.filter(function(v){ return v.age_hours >= 48; }).map(function(v){ return v.views; }).sort(function(x,y){ return x - y; }); if (!s.length) return true; var m = Math.floor(s.length / 2); return (s.length % 2 ? s[m] : (s[m-1] + s[m]) / 2) < 200; })($json.videos) }}

parameters.text:
=You are a YouTube channel analyst. You work only from the numbers below. You never claim to know retention, watch time, CTR or impressions — that data does not exist here.

CHANNEL
Name: {{ $('Prepare Channel Data').first().json.channel_title }}
Subscribers: {{ $('Prepare Channel Data').first().json.subs }}
Total videos on channel: {{ $('Prepare Channel Data').first().json.total_videos }}

SCALE
Median views per video: {{ $('Build Channel Fingerprint').first().json.median_views }}
Baseline views/hour: {{ $('Build Channel Fingerprint').first().json.baseline_vph }}  (= {{ $('Build Channel Fingerprint').first().json.baseline_views_per_day }} views/day)
Videos in baseline: {{ $('Build Channel Fingerprint').first().json.sample_size }}
NOISE FLOOR HIT: {{ $('Build Channel Fingerprint').first().json.noise_floor_hit }}

FINGERPRINT
{{ JSON.stringify($('Build Channel Fingerprint').first().json.fp) }}

ALL {{ $('Build Channel Fingerprint').first().json.videos.length }} UPLOADS
{{ JSON.stringify($('Build Channel Fingerprint').first().json.videos.map(function(v){ return {title: v.title, views: v.views, age_h: v.age_hours, mins: Math.round(v.duration_sec/60*10)/10, chapters: v.chapter_count, eng_per_1k: v.engagement_per_1k}; })) }}

Write a Telegram report in plain text under 320 words. No markdown, no preamble, no sign-off.

Use exactly these five headed sections, each heading on its own line:

CADENCE
Median days between uploads, the range, and days since the last upload. Say whether the schedule is consistent or erratic, and back it with the range.

FORMAT
Short (under 5 min) vs long (5 min+): the count and median views of each. Same for videos with 3+ chapters vs without. State which wins and by how much, or state that the split shows no difference. Give median title length.

TITLES
The percentage using first person, a number, and a tool name. Name the single best and worst performing video with their view counts and the spread between them. Say what the best-performing titles share in wording that the others do not.

TREND
Older half median views vs newer half median views. Say whether the channel is growing, flat, or declining, with both numbers.

DO THIS NEXT
Exactly three concrete actions, one line each, each tied to a number you cited above. No generic advice like "post consistently" or "improve thumbnails" unless a number in the data supports it.

ARITHMETIC RULES, these override everything:
- Use the numbers given. Never recompute a median. Never state a figure that is not derived from the data above.
- Every claim carries its number. "Long videos win" is banned; "long videos: 11 uploads, median 34 views vs short: 4 uploads, median 12" is required.
- If NOISE FLOOR HIT is true, add one line at the very top: the median is only {{ $('Build Channel Fingerprint').first().json.median_views }} views per video, so differences between videos are noise and nothing below should be read as proof of cause. Then still complete all five sections — structure, cadence and titles are readable at any scale.
- If a comparison group has fewer than 3 videos, say the group is too small instead of comparing it.

nodes.name: Build Channel Fingerprint
nodes.notes: Cadence, engagement ratios, trend, format splits, title patterns. Ratios work at any channel size; multiples do not.

assignments.name: fp
assignments.value: ={{ (function(vs, subs){   function med(a){ if(!a.length) return 0; var s=a.slice().sort(function(x,y){return x-y;}); var m=Math.floor(s.length/2); return s.length%2 ? s[m] : (s[m-1]+s[m])/2; }   var byDate = vs.slice().sort(function(a,b){ return new Date(a.published_at) - new Date(b.published_at); });   var gaps = []; for (var i=1;i<byDate.length;i++){ gaps.push((new Date(byDate[i].published_at) - new Date(byDate[i-1].published_at))/86400000); }   var eligible = vs.filter(function(v){ return v.age_hours >= 48; });   var half = Math.floor(byDate.length/2), older = byDate.slice(0,half), newer = byDate.slice(half);   var shortV = eligible.filter(function(v){ return v.duration_sec < 300; });   var longV = eligible.filter(function(v){ return v.duration_sec >= 300; });   var withCh = eligible.filter(function(v){ return v.chapter_count >= 3; });   var noCh = eligible.filter(function(v){ return v.chapter_count < 3; });   var titles = vs.map(function(v){ return v.title; });   var best = eligible.slice().sort(function(a,b){ return b.views-a.views; })[0] || {};   var worst = eligible.slice().sort(function(a,b){ return a.views-b.views; })[0] || {};   return {     days_since_last_upload: byDate.length ? Math.round((Date.now()-new Date(byDate[byDate.length-1].published_at))/86400000) : 0,     median_days_between_uploads: Math.round(med(gaps)*10)/10,     cadence_range: gaps.length ? (Math.round(Math.min.apply(null,gaps)*10)/10)+' to '+(Math.round(Math.max.apply(null,gaps)*10)/10)+' days' : 'n/a',     median_engagement_per_1k: med(eligible.map(function(v){ return v.engagement_per_1k; })),     median_views_per_100_subs: subs ? Math.round(med(eligible.map(function(v){ return v.views; }))/subs*1000)/10 : 0,     newer_half_median_views: Math.round(med(newer.map(function(v){ return v.views; }))),     older_half_median_views: Math.round(med(older.map(function(v){ return v.views; }))),     short_under5min: { n: shortV.length, median_views: Math.round(med(shortV.map(function(v){ return v.views; }))) },     long_over5min: { n: longV.length, median_views: Math.round(med(longV.map(function(v){ return v.views; }))) },     with_chapters: { n: withCh.length, median_views: Math.round(med(withCh.map(function(v){ return v.views; }))) },     without_chapters: { n: noCh.length, median_views: Math.round(med(noCh.map(function(v){ return v.views; }))) },     median_title_len: Math.round(med(vs.map(function(v){ return v.title_len; }))),     pct_titles_first_person: titles.length ? Math.round(titles.filter(function(t){ return /\b(I|My|Me)\b/.test(t); }).length/titles.length*100) : 0,     pct_titles_with_number: titles.length ? Math.round(titles.filter(function(t){ return /\d/.test(t); }).length/titles.length*100) : 0,     pct_titles_naming_tool: titles.length ? Math.round(titles.filter(function(t){ return /n8n|AI|GPT|Gemini|Claude|Python|API|Automat/i.test(t); }).length/titles.length*100) : 0,     best: { title: best.title || '', views: best.views || 0 },     worst: { title: worst.title || '', views: worst.views || 0 },     spread_ratio: (worst.views && best.views) ? Math.round(best.views/worst.views*10)/10 : 0   }; })($json.videos, $('Prepare Channel Data').first().json.subs) }}
